title: Describir cambios a lo largo del tiempo / Describing changes over time
bridge: In Spanish we use 'antes... ahora...', 'hace diez años...' or 'cada vez más...' to describe how something has changed. In French it works exactly the same with parallel structures: Avant.../Maintenant..., Il y a dix ans..., Ça a beaucoup changé, De plus en plus...
rule: To describe changes over time in French, we use temporal contrasts (Avant / Maintenant), references to the past with 'il y a + time', the expression 'ça a changé' with the passé composé for completed changes, and the construction 'de plus en plus + adjective/adverb' for progressive changes. The imperfect describes the previous situation and the present describes the current situation.

concept_examples.text: Avant, je prenais le bus. Maintenant, je vais au travail à vélo.
concept_examples.translation: Before, I took the bus. Now I go to work by bike.
concept_examples.phonetic: a.vɑ̃ ʒə pʁə.nɛ lə bys. mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃ ʒə vɛ o tʁa.vaj a ve.lo

concept_examples.text: Il y a dix ans, ce quartier était très calme. Ça a beaucoup changé.
concept_examples.translation: Ten years ago, this neighborhood was very quiet. It has changed a lot.
concept_examples.phonetic: il ja di zɑ̃ sə kaʁ.tje e.tɛ tʁɛ kalm. sa a bo.ku ʃɑ̃.ʒe

concept_examples.text: Les gens voyagent de plus en plus loin.
concept_examples.translation: People travel farther and farther.
concept_examples.phonetic: le ʒɑ̃ vwa.jaʒ də ply zɑ̃ ply lwɛ̃

common_error.wrong: Avant, je suis allé au bureau en bus.
common_error.correct: Avant, j'allais au bureau en bus.
common_error.explanation: To describe a habitual or continuous situation in the past, we use the imperfect (j'allais), not the passé composé (je suis allé). The passé composé indicates a punctual and finished action, while the imperfect describes past states or habits.

examples.original: Avant, j'habitais à la campagne. Maintenant, je vis en ville.
examples.phonetic: a.vɑ̃ ʒa.bi.tɛ a la kɑ̃.paɲ. mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃ ʒə vi ɑ̃ vil
examples.translation: Before, I lived in the countryside. Now I live in the city.
examples.note: Imperfect (habitais) for habitual past, present (vis) for current situation.

examples.original: Avant, tout était moins cher. Maintenant, les prix ont augmenté.
examples.phonetic: a.vɑ̃ tut e.tɛ mwɛ̃ ʃɛʁ. mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃ le pʁi ɔ̃ oɡ.mɑ̃.te
examples.translation: Before, everything was cheaper. Now prices have gone up.
examples.note: You can combine the imperfect for the past and the passé composé for a recent change.

levels.label: Il y a... ans / Ça a beaucoup changé
levels.translation: ... years ago / It has changed a lot

examples.original: Il y a vingt ans, on n'avait pas de smartphones. Ça a vraiment tout changé.
examples.phonetic: il ja vɛ̃ zɑ̃ ɔ̃ na.vɛ pa də smaʁt.fon. sa a vʁɛ.mɑ̃ tu ʃɑ̃.ʒe
examples.translation: Twenty years ago, we didn't have smartphones. It really changed everything.
examples.note: 'Il y a + time' always goes with a past reference. 'Ça a changé' uses the passé composé.

examples.original: Il y a cinq ans, ce restaurant n'existait pas. Il a beaucoup changé le quartier.
examples.phonetic: il ja sɛ̃k ɑ̃ sə ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃ nek.zis.tɛ pa. il a bo.ku ʃɑ̃.ʒe lə kaʁ.tje
examples.translation: Five years ago, this restaurant didn't exist. It has changed the neighborhood a lot.
examples.note: 'N'existait pas' uses the imperfect for a continuous past situation.

levels.label: De plus en plus / De moins en moins
levels.translation: More and more / Less and less

examples.original: Les hivers deviennent de plus en plus doux et les étés de plus en plus chauds.
examples.phonetic: le zi.vɛʁ də.vjɛn də ply zɑ̃ ply du e le ze.te də ply zɑ̃ ply ʃo
examples.translation: Winters are becoming milder and milder and summers hotter and hotter.
examples.note: 'De plus en plus + adjective' expresses a progressive and continuous change.

examples.original: On lit de moins en moins de journaux papier. Les gens préfèrent les informations en ligne.
examples.phonetic: ɔ̃ li də mwɛ̃ zɑ̃ mwɛ̃ də ʒuʁ.no pa.pje. le ʒɑ̃ pʁe.fɛʁ le ɛ̃.fɔʁ.ma.sjɔ̃ ɑ̃ liɲ
examples.translation: People read fewer and fewer paper newspapers. They prefer online news.
examples.note: 'De moins en moins' is the opposite of 'de plus en plus': it indicates a progressive decrease.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu as vu comme ce quartier a changé ?
dialogue.translation: Have you seen how this neighborhood has changed?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui ! Il y a dix ans, il y avait très peu de cafés ici.
dialogue.translation: Yes! Ten years ago, there were very few cafés here.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Avant, c'était un quartier industriel. Maintenant, c'est plein de boutiques tendance.
dialogue.translation: Before, it was an industrial neighborhood. Now it's full of trendy shops.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Et les loyers deviennent de plus en plus chers. Ça a vraiment beaucoup changé.
dialogue.translation: And rents are becoming more and more expensive. It has really changed a lot.

title: Especular y hacer deducciones / Speculating and making deductions
bridge: In Spanish we speculate with 'debe de ser...', 'debería...', 'quizás...', 'es probable que...' In French there is the same range of possibilities with different degrees of certainty: 'Il doit...' (high probability), 'Il se peut que...' (possibility), 'Peut-être que...' (maybe), 'C'est probablement...' (general probability).
rule: Deductions and speculations in French are expressed with various resources depending on the degree of certainty: (1) 'Devoir + infinitif' in the present for logical assumption (equivalent to 'debe de...'); (2) 'Il se peut que + subjonctif' for possibility (equivalent to 'puede que...'); (3) 'Peut-être que + indicatif' or 'peut-être + inversion' for conjecture; (4) adverbs like 'probablement', 'certainement', 'sûrement' modify the verb. The subjunctive is obligatory after 'il se peut que' and other expressions of possibility/doubt.

concept_examples.text: Il doit être fatigué — il travaille depuis douze heures.
concept_examples.translation: He must be tired: he has been working for twelve hours.
concept_examples.phonetic: il dwa ɛ.tʁə fa.ti.ɡe il tʁa.vaj də.pɥi duz œʁ

concept_examples.text: Il se peut qu'elle soit déjà arrivée.
concept_examples.translation: She may have already arrived.
concept_examples.phonetic: il sə pø kɛl swa de.ʒa a.ʁi.ve

concept_examples.text: C'est probablement une erreur de traduction.
concept_examples.translation: It's probably a translation error.
concept_examples.phonetic: sɛ pʁo.bab.lə.mɑ̃ yn e.ʁœʁ də tʁa.dyk.sjɔ̃

common_error.wrong: Il se peut qu'elle est déjà arrivée.
common_error.correct: Il se peut qu'elle soit déjà arrivée.
common_error.explanation: After 'il se peut que' it is obligatory to use the subjunctive (soit), not the indicative (est). If you want to avoid the subjunctive you can rephrase with 'peut-être que' + indicative, which is more common in colloquial speech.

examples.original: Peut-être qu'il a raté son train.
examples.phonetic: pø.tɛtʁ kil a ʁa.te sɔ̃ tʁɛ̃
examples.translation: Maybe he missed his train.
examples.note: 'Peut-être que' + indicative is the most common and simple way to speculate.

examples.original: C'est probablement la meilleure solution.
examples.phonetic: sɛ pʁo.bab.lə.mɑ̃ la mɛ.jœʁ so.ly.sjɔ̃
examples.translation: It's probably the best solution.
examples.note: The adverb 'probablement' goes between the auxiliary verb and the participle, or before the main verb.

examples.original: Elle ne répond pas. Elle doit dormir.
examples.phonetic: ɛl nə ʁe.pɔ̃ pa. ɛl dwa dɔʁ.miʁ
examples.translation: She isn't answering. She must be sleeping.
examples.note: 'Devoir' in the present + infinitive expresses a logical assumption of high probability.

examples.original: Ce paquet doit peser au moins cinq kilos.
examples.phonetic: sə pa.kɛ dwa pə.ze o mwɛ̃ sɛ̃k ki.lo
examples.translation: This package must weigh at least five kilos.
examples.note: The deduction is based on observable evidence or logical reasoning.

levels.label: Il se peut que + subjonctif / Il devrait...

examples.original: Il se peut que la réunion soit annulée à cause de la grève.
examples.phonetic: il sə pø kə la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ swa a.ny.le a koz də la ɡʁɛv
examples.translation: The meeting may be canceled because of the strike.
examples.note: Subjunctive is obligatory (soit) after 'il se peut que'. It expresses real but uncertain possibility.

examples.original: Il devrait arriver vers dix-neuf heures, sauf imprévu.
examples.phonetic: il də.vʁɛ a.ʁi.ve vɛʁ diz.nœv œʁ sof ɛ̃.pʁe.vy
examples.translation: He should arrive around seven o'clock, unless something unexpected comes up.
examples.note: 'Devrait' (conditional of devoir) expresses expectation or assumption with reservations.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Marc n'est pas encore là. Qu'est-ce qui se passe, à ton avis ?
dialogue.translation: Marc isn't here yet. What's going on, in your opinion?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Il doit être coincé dans les embouteillages. Il y a toujours des bouchons le vendredi soir.
dialogue.translation: He must be stuck in traffic. There are always jams on Friday evening.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Il se peut qu'il ait aussi oublié notre rendez-vous.
dialogue.translation: He may have also forgotten our appointment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Peut-être, mais c'est peu probable. Il est toujours très ponctuel. Il devrait arriver d'une minute à l'autre.
dialogue.translation: Maybe, but it's unlikely. He is always very punctual. He should arrive any minute now.

title: Expresar arrepentimiento e hipótesis irreales / Expressing regret and unreal hypotheses
bridge: In Spanish we say 'si hubiera sabido...', 'debería haber...', 'ojalá hubiera...' to express regret or imagine an alternative past. In French these ideas are expressed with the conditionnel passé, the plus-que-parfait in 'si' clauses, and fixed expressions like 'Si seulement...' or 'Je regrette de ne pas avoir...'
rule: Unreal hypotheses about the past in French follow the pattern: SI + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé. The plus-que-parfait is formed with avoir/être in the imperfect + past participle. The conditionnel passé is formed with avoir/être in the conditional + past participle. 'J'aurais dû + infinitif' is equivalent to 'should have...'. 'Si seulement...' expresses an impossible wish about the past and can be followed by the plus-que-parfait. 'Je regrette de ne pas avoir + infinitif passé' is the standard formula for regret.

concept_examples.text: Si j'avais su, je n'aurais pas accepté ce travail.
concept_examples.translation: If I had known, I would not have accepted this job.
concept_examples.phonetic: si ʒa.vɛ sy ʒə no.ʁɛ pa ak.sɛp.te sə tʁa.vaj

concept_examples.text: J'aurais dû partir plus tôt pour éviter les embouteillages.
concept_examples.translation: I should have left earlier to avoid the traffic jams.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒo.ʁɛ dy paʁ.tiʁ ply to puʁ e.vi.te le zɑ̃.bu.tɛ.jaʒ

concept_examples.text: Je regrette de ne pas avoir étudié davantage.
concept_examples.translation: I regret not having studied more.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒə ʁə.ɡʁɛt də nə pa za.vwaʁ e.ty.dje da.vɑ̃.taʒ

common_error.wrong: Si j'aurais su, je n'aurais pas accepté.
common_error.correct: Si j'avais su, je n'aurais pas accepté.
common_error.explanation: In French, the 'si' clause expressing an unreal condition in the past can NEVER take the conditional — it always takes the plus-que-parfait (j'avais su). The conditionnel passé (j'aurais su) only goes in the result clause, never in the 'si' clause.

levels.label: J'aurais dû... / Je regrette de ne pas avoir...
levels.translation: I should have... / I regret not having...

examples.original: J'aurais dû appeler avant de venir.
examples.phonetic: ʒo.ʁɛ dy a.pə.le a.vɑ̃ də və.niʁ
examples.translation: I should have called before coming.
examples.note: 'Aurais dû + infinitif' is the most direct way to express regret for not having done something.

examples.original: Je regrette de ne pas avoir pris de photos pendant le voyage.
examples.phonetic: ʒə ʁə.ɡʁɛt də nə pa za.vwaʁ pʁi də fo.to pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə vwa.jaʒ
examples.translation: I regret not having taken photos during the trip.
examples.note: The structure is: regretter de + ne pas avoir + past participle. The negation goes before the auxiliary infinitive.

levels.label: Si seulement...
levels.translation: If only... / I wish I had...

examples.original: Si seulement j'avais écouté mes parents !
examples.phonetic: si sœl.mɑ̃ ʒa.vɛ ze.ku.te me pa.ʁɑ̃
examples.translation: If only I had listened to my parents!
examples.note: 'Si seulement' + plus-que-parfait expresses an impossible wish about the past, with a tone of lament.

examples.original: Si seulement nous avions eu plus de temps pour préparer le projet !
examples.phonetic: si sœl.mɑ̃ nu za.vjɔ̃ zy ply də tɑ̃ puʁ pʁe.pa.ʁe lə pʁo.ʒɛ
examples.translation: If only we had had more time to prepare the project!
examples.note: You can also use 'si seulement' without a verb or with the imperfect for wishes about the present.

examples.original: Si tu m'avais prévenu, j'aurais pu t'aider.
examples.phonetic: si ty ma.vɛ pʁe.vœ.ny ʒo.ʁɛ py te.de
examples.translation: If you had warned me, I could have helped you.
examples.note: Classic pattern: 'si' + past perfect (m'avais prévenu) → past conditional (aurais pu).

examples.original: Si elle avait choisi une autre carrière, elle aurait été plus heureuse.
examples.phonetic: si ɛl a.vɛ ʃwa.zi yn o.tʁ ka.ʁjɛʁ ɛl o.ʁɛ e.te ply ø.ʁøz
examples.translation: If she had chosen another career, she would have been happier.
examples.note: With 'être' in the past conditional: 'aurait été'. The adjective agrees with the subject (heureuse).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu as l'air déprimé. Qu'est-ce qui t'arrive ?
dialogue.translation: You look depressed. What's happening to you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: J'ai raté mon examen. J'aurais dû réviser plus sérieusement.
dialogue.translation: I failed my exam. I should have studied more seriously.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Si seulement tu m'avais dit que tu avais des difficultés, j'aurais pu t'aider.
dialogue.translation: If only you had told me you were having difficulties, I could have helped you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je sais. Je regrette de ne pas avoir demandé de l'aide plus tôt. C'est trop tard maintenant.
dialogue.translation: I know. I regret not having asked for help earlier. It's too late now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ce n'est pas grave. Si tu avais échoué l'année dernière, tu te serais préparé différemment. C'est une leçon pour la prochaine fois.
dialogue.translation: It's not serious. If you had failed last year, you would have prepared differently. It's a lesson for next time.

title: Exprimer les avantages et les inconvénients / Expressing advantages and disadvantages
bridge: In Spanish, we usually use 'ventaja' and 'inconveniente' with connectors like 'por un lado... por otro lado'. In French, the equivalents are 'avantage' and 'inconvénient', but be careful: 'inconvénient' is pronounced with a nasal sound and has no accent. Also remember that in French, 'c'est vrai que' is often used with the subjunctive in the subordinate clause, whereas in Spanish we use the indicative: 'Es verdad que es caro' → 'C'est vrai que ce soit cher' (trap!).
rule: To express advantages and disadvantages in French, use: 'avantage' (advantage) and 'inconvénient' (disadvantage). To introduce them, you can use: 'l'avantage, c'est que...' (the advantage is that), 'l'inconvénient, c'est que...' (the disadvantage is that). Also common are 'd'un côté... de l'autre côté' (on one hand... on the other hand), 'par contre' (on the other hand, however) and 'cependant' (however). To give your opinion, use 'à mon avis' (in my opinion) or 'je pense que' (I think that). Remember that 'que' requires the subjunctive when the main clause expresses a negative opinion or doubt: 'Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée' (I don't think it's a good idea). At B1 level, master these structures with the indicative and subjunctive.

concept_examples.text: L'avantage, c'est que c'est très pratique.
concept_examples.translation: The advantage is that it is very practical.
concept_examples.phonetic: lavɑ̃taʒ sɛ kə sɛ tʁɛ pʁatik

concept_examples.text: L'inconvénient, c'est que ça coûte cher.
concept_examples.translation: The disadvantage is that it costs a lot.
concept_examples.phonetic: lɛ̃kɔ̃venjɑ̃ sɛ kə sa kut ʃɛʁ

concept_examples.text: D'un côté, c'est rapide, mais de l'autre côté, c'est risqué.
concept_examples.translation: On one hand, it's fast, but on the other hand, it's risky.
concept_examples.phonetic: dœ̃ kote sɛ ʁapid mɛ də lotʁ kote sɛ ʁiske

concept_examples.text: À mon avis, les avantages l'emportent sur les inconvénients.
concept_examples.translation: In my opinion, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
concept_examples.phonetic: a mɔ̃navi lezɑ̃vɑ̃taʒ lɑ̃pɔʁt syʁ lezɛ̃kɔ̃venjɑ̃

common_error.wrong: Il y a beaucoup d'avantages, mais aussi des désavantages.
common_error.correct: Il y a beaucoup d'avantages, mais aussi des inconvénients.
common_error.correct_alt: Il y a beaucoup d'avantages, mais aussi des points négatifs.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, we say 'desventajas' or 'desventajas', but in French you don't say 'désavantages' to refer to disadvantages (although the word exists, 'inconvénients' is used more). The error comes from a direct calque from Spanish. To avoid it, remember that 'inconvénient' is the most common and natural term in French.

examples.original: L'avantage principal, c'est la flexibilité.
examples.phonetic: lavɑ̃taʒ pʁɛ̃sipɑl sɛ la flɛksibilite
examples.translation: The main advantage is flexibility.
examples.note: Use 'l'avantage principal' to highlight the most important advantage. Remember that 'c'est' agrees with the singular noun.

examples.original: Un autre avantage, c'est qu'on gagne du temps.
examples.phonetic: œ̃n otʁ avɑ̃taʒ sɛ kɔ̃ gaɲ dy tɑ̃
examples.translation: Another advantage is that you save time.
examples.note: 'Un autre avantage' is common. Note that 'on' is used for 'we' or 'people'.

examples.original: Le point positif, c'est que c'est facile à utiliser.
examples.phonetic: lə pwɛ̃ pɔzitif sɛ kə sɛ fasil a ytize
examples.translation: The positive point is that it is easy to use.
examples.note: 'Le point positif' is a synonym for 'avantage'. Here 'que' is followed by the indicative because the main clause is affirmative.

examples.original: L'inconvénient, c'est que c'est cher.
examples.phonetic: lɛ̃kɔ̃venjɑ̃ sɛ kə sɛ ʃɛʁ
examples.translation: The disadvantage is that it is expensive.
examples.note: Typical structure: 'L'inconvénient, c'est que...' + indicative. Don't forget the nasal sound.

examples.original: Le problème, c'est que ça prend du temps.
examples.phonetic: lə pʁɔblɛm sɛ kə sa pʁɑ̃ dy tɑ̃
examples.translation: The problem is that it takes time.
examples.note: 'Le problème' is another way to introduce a disadvantage. 'Prendre du temps' means 'to take time'.

examples.original: Par contre, ça peut être dangereux.
examples.phonetic: paʁ kɔ̃tʁ sa pø ɛtʁ dɑ̃ʒø
examples.translation: On the other hand, it can be dangerous.
examples.note: 'Par contre' is used to contrast and is very common in spoken French. Note that 'peut' is the conjugated verb 'pouvoir'.

examples.original: D'un côté, c'est économique, mais de l'autre, c'est moins fiable.
examples.phonetic: dœ̃ kote sɛ ekonomi mɛ də lotʁ sɛ mwɛ̃ fjabl
examples.translation: On one hand, it's economical, but on the other, it's less reliable.
examples.note: Structure 'd'un côté... de l'autre' to contrast two aspects. Note that 'moins' means 'less'.

examples.original: Bien que ce soit plus cher, c'est plus durable.
examples.phonetic: bjɛ̃ kə sə swa ply ʃɛʁ sɛ ply dyʁabl
examples.translation: Although it is more expensive, it is more durable.
examples.note: 'Bien que' requires the subjunctive: 'ce soit'. It is a common mistake to use the indicative. Remember that in French, 'bien que' always takes the subjunctive.

examples.original: Malgré les inconvénients, je pense que c'est une bonne idée.
examples.phonetic: malɡʁe lezɛ̃kɔ̃venjɑ̃ ʒə pɑ̃s kə sɛt‿yn bɔn ide
examples.translation: Despite the disadvantages, I think it's a good idea.
examples.note: 'Malgré' is a preposition meaning 'despite' and is followed by a noun (not a verb).

examples.original: Les avantages l'emportent sur les inconvénients.
examples.phonetic: lezɑ̃vɑ̃taʒ lɑ̃pɔʁt syʁ lezɛ̃kɔ̃venjɑ̃
examples.translation: The advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
examples.note: Idiomatic expression: 'l'emporter sur' = 'to outweigh, to prevail'.

translations.en: Advantages and disadvantages of an idea

title: Raconter une histoire / Telling a story or anecdote
bridge: In French, to narrate in the past, two main tenses are used: the passé composé for specific actions and the imparfait for descriptions or habitual actions. In Spanish, this distinction exists between the pretérito indefinido and the pretérito imperfecto, but the passé composé is formed with the auxiliaries avoir or être, whereas in Spanish we use a single verb form. Additionally, in French, the past participle may agree with the subject when être is used.
rule: To narrate a story in French at B1 level, the passé composé and the imparfait are combined. The passé composé is formed with the present tense of avoir or être + past participle. With être, the participle agrees in gender and number with the subject (e.g., elle est partie). The imparfait is formed with the root of the nous form in the present tense + endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. It is used for descriptions, ongoing actions, habits, and background situations. Tense agreement is key: the imparfait sets the context and the passé composé introduces specific actions. Additionally, temporal connectors such as 'd'abord', 'ensuite', 'puis', 'finalement' are used to sequence events. Exception: some verbs of movement (aller, venir, partir, arriver) and reflexive verbs use être.

concept_examples.text: Hier, je suis allé au marché et j'ai acheté des légumes.
concept_examples.translation: Yesterday I went to the market and bought vegetables.
concept_examples.phonetic: /jɛʁ ʒə sɥi‿zale o maʁʃe e ʒe‿aʃte de leɡym/

concept_examples.text: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais au parc avec mes amis.
concept_examples.translation: When I was little, I used to play in the park with my friends.
concept_examples.phonetic: /kɑ̃ ʒetɛ pəti ʒə ʒwɛ o paʁk avɛk mez‿ami/

concept_examples.text: Il faisait beau, alors nous avons décidé de faire une promenade.
concept_examples.translation: The weather was nice, so we decided to take a walk.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fəzɛ bo alɔʁ nu‿zavɔ̃ deside də fɛʁ yn pʁɔmənad/

concept_examples.text: Elle est arrivée en retard parce qu'elle avait raté son bus.
concept_examples.translation: She arrived late because she had missed her bus.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛl e‿taʁive ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ paʁsk‿ɛl avɛ ʁate sɔ̃ bys/

common_error.wrong: Hier, je suis allé au marché et j'ai acheté des légumes.
common_error.correct: Hier, je suis allé au marché et j'ai acheté des légumes.
common_error.explanation: This example does not contain an error; it is correct. However, a typical error among Spanish speakers is omitting the agreement of the past participle with the auxiliary être, for example saying 'Elle est arrivé' instead of 'Elle est arrivée'. Another error is using the passé composé for habitual descriptions, such as 'Quand j'étais petit, j'ai joué au parc' instead of 'je jouais'. To avoid this, remember that the imparfait describes the context and repeated actions, and the passé composé is for specific actions.

levels.label: Les temps du passé / Los tiempos del pasado

examples.original: J'ai mangé une pomme.
examples.phonetic: /ʒe mɑ̃ʒe yn pɔm/
examples.translation: I ate an apple.
examples.note: Use of the passé composé for a specific and completed action.

examples.original: Je mangeais une pomme quand il est arrivé.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə mɑ̃ʒɛ yn pɔm kɑ̃ il e‿taʁive/
examples.translation: I was eating an apple when he arrived.
examples.note: The imparfait describes the ongoing action; the passé composé interrupts.

examples.original: Quand j'étais enfant, je jouais au foot.
examples.phonetic: /kɑ̃ ʒetɛ ɑ̃fɑ̃ ʒə ʒwɛ o fut/
examples.translation: When I was a child, I used to play soccer.
examples.note: The imparfait for habitual actions in the past.

levels.label: La structure du récit / La estructura del relato

examples.original: D'abord, je me suis levé tôt.
examples.phonetic: /dabɔʁ ʒə mə sɥi ləve to/
examples.translation: First, I got up early.
examples.note: Use of connectors to start the narration.

examples.original: Ensuite, j'ai pris mon petit-déjeuner.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃sɥit ʒe pʁi mɔ̃ pəti deʒøne/
examples.translation: Then, I had breakfast.
examples.note: Use of 'ensuite' to sequence actions.

examples.original: Finalement, nous sommes partis au cinéma.
examples.phonetic: /finalmɑ̃ nu sɔm paʁti o sinema/
examples.translation: Finally, we left to the cinema.
examples.note: Agreement of the participle with 'nous' and use of 'finalement'.

levels.label: La concordance des temps / La concordancia de tiempos

examples.original: Pendant que je lisais, le téléphone a sonné.
examples.phonetic: /pɑ̃dɑ̃ kə ʒə lizɛ lə telefɔn a sɔne/
examples.translation: While I was reading, the phone rang.
examples.note: Imparfait for the background action, passé composé for the interruption.

examples.original: Il pleuvait, donc nous sommes restés à la maison.
examples.phonetic: /il pløvɛ dɔ̃k nu sɔm ʁɛste a la mɛzɔ̃/
examples.translation: It was raining, so we stayed at home.
examples.note: The imparfait describes the weather, the passé composé the resulting action.

examples.original: Elle s'est couchée après qu'elle a fini ses devoirs.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl se kuʃe apʁɛ kɛl a fini se dəvwaʁ/
examples.translation: She went to bed after she finished her homework.
examples.note: Use of 'après que' with the indicative, and agreement of the participle with 'elle'.

title: Argumenter un point de vue / Argue a point of view
bridge: In Spanish we use 'creo que', 'pienso que', and 'estoy de acuerdo' to express opinions. In French, the structure is similar, but there are important differences: the verb 'penser' requires the preposition 'que' (pienso que → je pense que), and 'être d'accord' is used without 'que' when you simply agree with someone (estoy de acuerdo → je suis d'accord). Also, in French, negation with 'ne...pas' surrounds the verb, and this affects expressions like 'je ne pense pas que' (no creo que), which also introduces the subjunctive — a concept we use similarly in Spanish, but with nuances. Be careful with the position of pronouns and with the use of 'si' (if) which does not carry an accent in French.
rule:
To argue a point of view in French at B1 level, use these structures:

- **Express opinion**: 'Je pense que' (I think that), 'Je crois que' (I believe that), 'À mon avis' (in my opinion), 'Selon moi' (according to me). After these expressions, use the indicative if the opinion is affirmative. Example: 'Je pense qu'il a raison.' (I think he is right.)

- **Express disagreement**: 'Je ne suis pas d'accord' (I disagree), 'Je ne pense pas que' (I don't think that). After the negative form of 'penser' or 'croire', use the subjunctive: 'Je ne pense pas qu'il ait raison.' (I don't think he is right.)

- **Give reasons**: 'parce que' (because), 'car' (since, as), 'à cause de' (due to) + noun, 'grâce à' (thanks to) + noun. Example: 'Je suis contre cette idée parce qu'elle est trop coûteuse.' (I am against this idea because it is too costly.)

- **Counter-argue**: 'Cependant' (however), 'toutefois' (nevertheless), 'par contre' (on the other hand). Example: 'C'est une bonne idée, cependant il y a des risques.' (It's a good idea, however there are risks.)

- **Concede a point**: 'Certes' (certainly), 'Il est vrai que' (it is true that). Example: 'Il est vrai que le projet est ambitieux.' (It is true that the project is ambitious.)

- **Conclude**: 'En conclusion' (in conclusion), 'Pour conclure' (to conclude), 'Donc' (therefore). Example: 'Donc, je pense que nous devrions agir.' (Therefore, I think we should act.)

Remember: in French, after 'que' use the indicative or subjunctive depending on the verb and negation. Learn to distinguish these cases.

concept_examples.text: Je pense que c'est une excellente idée.
concept_examples.translation: I think it's an excellent idea.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə sɛ.t‿ɛ̃.n‿ɛk.sɛ.lɑ̃t i.de/
concept_examples.note: Use of 'penser que' with indicative (es: c'est)

concept_examples.text: Je ne suis pas d'accord avec toi.
concept_examples.translation: I don't agree with you.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɥi pa d‿a.kɔʁ a.vɛk twa/
concept_examples.note: Expression of disagreement without 'que', followed by 'avec' + person

concept_examples.text: À mon avis, il faut réduire les dépenses.
concept_examples.translation: In my opinion, we need to reduce expenses.
concept_examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃.n‿a.vi il fo ʁe.dɥiʁ le de.pɑ̃s/
concept_examples.note: Use of 'à mon avis' + impersonal verb 'falloir' (il faut)

concept_examples.text: Je ne pense pas qu'il ait raison.
concept_examples.translation: I don't think he is right.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa k‿il ɛ ʁɛ.zɔ̃/
concept_examples.note: Negation + 'penser que' requires subjunctive ('ait' is subjunctive of 'avoir')

common_error.wrong: Je suis d'accord que tu as raison.
common_error.correct: Je suis d'accord avec toi / Je suis d'accord pour dire que tu as raison.
common_error.correct_alt: Je suis d'accord sur ce point.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish we say 'estoy de acuerdo en que', but in French 'être d'accord' is constructed with 'avec' (with someone) or 'pour + infinitive' / 'pour dire que'. 'que' is not used directly after 'd'accord'. To talk about an opinion, you say 'Je suis d'accord pour dire que...' or simply 'Je suis d'accord avec toi.'

examples.original: Je crois que ce film est intéressant.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə kʁwa kə sə film ɛ.t‿ɛ̃.te.ʁɛ.sɑ̃/
examples.translation: I believe this movie is interesting.
examples.note: Use of 'croire que' with indicative (est).

examples.original: Selon moi, cette solution est la meilleure.
examples.phonetic: /sə.lɔ̃ mwa sɛt sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ ɛ la mɛ.jœʁ/
examples.translation: According to me, this solution is the best.
examples.note: Expression 'selon moi' followed by a statement.

examples.original: À mon avis, il a tort.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃.n‿a.vi il a tɔʁ/
examples.translation: In my opinion, he is wrong.
examples.note: Use of 'à mon avis' and 'avoir tort'.

examples.original: Je ne suis pas d'accord avec cette décision.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɥi pa d‿a.kɔʁ a.vɛk sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I don't agree with this decision.
examples.note: Direct disagreement with 'avec'.

examples.original: Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sə swa.t‿yn bɔ.n‿i.de/
examples.translation: I don't think it's a good idea.
examples.note: Subjunctive after negation of 'penser'.

examples.original: Tu as raison, mais je ne suis pas tout à fait d'accord.
examples.phonetic: /ty a ʁɛ.zɔ̃ mɛ ʒə nə sɥi pa tu.t‿a fɛ d‿a.kɔʁ/
examples.translation: You're right, but I don't entirely agree.
examples.note: Use of 'mais' to qualify.

examples.original: Certes, c'est cher, mais cela en vaut la peine.
examples.phonetic: /sɛʁt sɛ ʃɛʁ mɛ sə.la ɑ̃ vo la pɛn/
examples.translation: Certainly, it's expensive, but it's worth it.
examples.note: Structure 'Certes... mais' to concede and counter-argue.

examples.original: Il est vrai que le projet est ambitieux, cependant il est réalisable.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ vʁɛ kə lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.bi.sjø sə.pɑ̃.dɑ̃ il ɛ ʁe.a.li.zabl/
examples.translation: It's true that the project is ambitious, however it is feasible.
examples.note: Use of 'il est vrai que' + 'cependant'.

examples.original: Par contre, cette solution est plus rapide.
examples.phonetic: /paʁ kɔ̃tʁ sɛt sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ ɛ ply ʁa.pid/
examples.translation: On the other hand, this solution is faster.
examples.note: 'Par contre' introduces a contrasting opinion.
